1.

Heard learned counsel for the applicant, learned Aga, learned counsel for the informant and
perused the record.
2.  The applicant seeks enlargement on bail in FIR No.0366 of 2020, under Section 498A, 304B IPC & Section 3/4 of Dowry Prohibition Act, P.S. Atariya, District Sitapur.
3. In terms of the allegation, the daughter of the informant was married on 14.05.2020 and was being asked for dowry and on 05.12.2020, the whole family had killed the daughter.
Learned counsel for the applicant draws my attention to the post-mortem on record which indicates only a Ankit Kumar @ Ankit vs State Of U.P. Thru Prin.Secy.

He argues that there is no document on record to demonstrate that soon before her death, she was subjected to physical or mental cruelty in relation to demand of dowry.

4. Learned counsel for the informant opposes the bail application by arguing that the death had occurred within six months of marriage and thus, the bail application should be rejected.
5.
Learned AGA has also opposed the bail application.

6. Considering the fact that there is no document on record to demonstrate that soon before her death, she was subjected to physical or mental cruelty in relation to demand of dowry coupled with the fact that the applicant has no criminal antecedent and is in custody since 31.03.2021, the applicant is entitled to be enlarged on bail.
In view thereof, the application is allowed.

7. Let the applicant Ankit Kumar @ Ankit be released on bail in aforesaid FIR number on his furnishing a personal bond with two sureties of Rs.25,000/- each to the satisfaction of court concerned with the following conditions:
(a) The applicant shall execute a bond to undertake to attend the hearings;
(b) The applicant shall not commit any offence similar to the offence of which he is accused or suspected of the commission; and (c) The applicant shall not directly or indirectly make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or to any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
8.
However, the trial Court is directed to expedite the trial and if possible, conclude the same within one year.
